title: Keyboard Reborn — CSS Keyboard, Synth & Typing Test
description: A realistic low-profile aluminum keyboard built entirely from CSS gradients and shadows that mirrors your physical keypresses, with a graphite finish option. Switch to synth mode to play it as a Web Audio instrument with waveforms, octave shift and an oscilloscope, or take a typing test that tracks WPM and accuracy.
prompt: Remake my old CSS Apple-style keyboard replica as 'Keyboard Reborn': a beautifully rendered, realistic aluminum low-profile keyboard in pure CSS — no images — where pressing keys on my physical keyboard animates the matching keys. Add a synth mode where the keys play notes through Web Audio (only after a user gesture), and a typing-speed test mode with WPM and accuracy. It has to be responsive: on phones the board scales down and the virtual keys are tappable. No brand logos, one self-contained HTML file.

methodology: Event mirroring: keyboard.down/up on letters, modifiers and arrows must toggle the matching key's .down class and update the last-key readout.
Pointer path: tapping virtual keys works on the touch profile and releases cleanly (no stuck keys).
Audio gating: the AudioContext must not exist until a key gesture; voices are counted through a small window hook and note frequencies are asserted as text.
Time-controlled typing test: page.clock pauses time so exactly 60 s separates the first and last keystroke, making WPM an exact oracle.
Typing error handling: wrong characters are marked, backspace corrects them, accuracy counts every keystroke, and Esc deals a new passage.
Visual review of both finishes at 1280px and 390px, plus reduced motion (flat board, no caret blink).
risks: Stuck keys when a keyup is swallowed (⌘ on macOS, window blur, pointer leaving a key).
Autoplay policy leaving the AudioContext suspended.
Space/Tab default actions scrolling the page or stealing focus mid-test.
Keys becoming too small to tap at 360px.
qa.playwright: Keyboard events are Playwright's strong suit: keyboard.down/up give precise control over held keys, which is exactly what the pressed-state animation needs. Audio can't be heard in CI, so the spec checks the gate (audioState 'none' before a gesture), live voice counts and the displayed pitch instead of sound. Timing was the tricky part: an installed but running clock still counted real typing latency, so the test uses page.clock.pauseAt() plus runFor(60_000) to make WPM deterministic. Typing about 110 characters through real key events is slow under load, so that one test gets a longer timeout and reduced motion to cut paint cost.
coverage: Tappable virtual keys and persisted finish toggle
Synth: gesture-gated audio, pitch mapping, octave shift
Typing test WPM/accuracy under a controlled clock
Typing mistakes, backspace and new passage

a11y: Modes are an ARIA tablist with arrow-key navigation, and every control is a native button with visible focus. The on-screen keys are real buttons kept out of the tab order because the physical keyboard is the primary input, and readouts sit in aria-live regions with the typing result announced as a status.
